title: Attention optimizer smoke and needle tests
body:
Purpose:
Quick, high-signal "needle" tests and smoke checks for attention kernel selection and prefetch behavior. Goal is to produce reproducible microcases that expose kernel-switch thrash, small-batch starvation, and prefetch hysteresis without running full workload suites.

Why this doc exists (context):
- We keep seeing intermittent 95th/99th latency spikes in mixed-length traffic. Hypothesis: frequent kernel handoffs between FlashAttention (fused path) and paged/flash-paged kernels when sequences cross thresholds + KV-cache pressure.
- Existing large notebooks are great for long runs; need short tests (30s–5m) that reliably trigger failure modes for devs and CI.

Hypotheses to test quickly:
1) Kernel flip flops when 1) seq_len distribution has a heavy tail and 2) batching coalescer mixes short and long requests, causing prefetch + fusion warmup thrash.
2) Small-batch coalescer misses for pulsey traffic cause single-request path to use non-fused ops more often, adding 5–20% p99.
3) Prefetch hysteresis config (prefetch_window_ms) tuned too conservatively — when bursts arrive within hysteresis window, we under-prefetch and cause IO stalls.

Quick checklist (smoke/needle):
- Repro recipe 1: Kernel flip (short run, high tail)
  - Runner: local dev node (A40), CUDA 11.8, runtime branch: pr/1427
  - Commands: run microdriver with workload config 'flip-20p-tail.yaml' (included below) for 3 minutes.
  - Expected: 3–6 kernel handoffs per second visible in trace; p95 increase ~10–30ms vs baseline.

- Repro recipe 2: Small-batch starvation
  - Runner: 4xA100 (local cluster), batcher enabled, coalescer delay set to 4ms
  - Commands: inject single-request bursts (qps=120 burst_len=1 every 8ms) for 5m
  - Expected: elevated single-request path usage (fusedops count down 35%), tail spikes at 99th.

- Repro recipe 3: Prefetch hysteresis gating
  - Runner: single Gaudi (or A100), set prefetch_window_ms=12 vs control 24
  - Commands: repeat burst pattern with rising intensity and measure GPU utilization + stalls
  - Expected: lower sustained utilization but more tail stalls when window too small.

Workload configs (examples)
flip-20p-tail.yaml:
  model: redwood-7b-quant-cpu-gpu
  seq_distribution: mix
    - 70%: seq_len=32
    - 20%: seq_len=256
    - 10%: seq_len=1024
  qps: 200
  duration_s: 180
  batcher: on
  coalescer_delay_ms: 6
  kv_cache: enabled

needle-single-burst.yaml:
  model: redwood-compat-3b
  seq_len: 64
  burst_pattern: single-pulse
    qps_peak: 120
    burst_interval_ms: 8
    duration_s: 300
  batcher: on
  coalescer_delay_ms: 4

Telemetry + traces to collect (minimum):
- per-request trace with kernel-choice annotation (tag kernel=fused|paged|flashpaged)
- GPU timeline (nsight) capture of 30s window centered on a spike
- runtime debug counters: fused_op_count, paged_invocations, kernel_handoffs, kv_evictions, prefetch_actions
- host perf: nvprof/metrics: sm_efficiency, achieved_occupancy, mem_copy_bytes
- aggregated: p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/s, GPU utilization

Quick shell snippets (dev friendly)
- start microdriver: ./bin/microdriver --cfg flip-20p-tail.yaml --runtime-image pr-1427 --traces=on --trace-out=/tmp/trace.json
- fetch kernel counters: curl -s localhost:9090/metrics | grep fused_op_count
- gdb attach (rare): sudo gdb --args ./runtime_worker --config ... (use only if native debug needed)

What to look for in traces (rules of thumb):
- Recurrent alternating kernel tags on consecutive requests with same seq_len -> suspicious handoff logic.
- Kernel handoff immediately followed by kv_eviction spikes -> plausibly memory-pressure-triggered fallback.
- Prefetch action count dropping to 0 during burst -> hysteresis prevented prefetch.
- If fused_op_count drops but GPU occupancy unchanged -> we lost kernel efficiency (latency likely up).

Representative (toy) trace excerpt (annotated):
TS 0.000s REQ 328 seq=1024 kernel=paged prefetch=miss kv_evictions=0
TS 0.012s REQ 329 seq=32   kernel=fused prefetch=hit  kv_evictions=0  <-- handoff from paged->fused in 12ms window
TS 0.025s REQ 330 seq=1024 kernel=flashpaged prefetch=miss kv_evictions=3  <-- eviction followed by flashpaged selection

Initial results (dev run A, 2025-11-22):
- flip-20p-tail (3m) on A40: p95 increased 14ms over baseline, fused_op_count fell 21% during spike windows, kernel_handoffs averaged 4/s.
- small-burst pattern (5m) on 4xA100: p99 delta +68ms when coalescer_delay_ms<=4; increasing delay to 8ms reduced p99 by ~30ms but p50 slightly worsened.
- prefetch_window_ms trial: 12ms gave lower steady utilization but doubled number of prefetch_miss events vs 24ms.

Actionable tuning ideas (short list):
- Increase coalescer_delay_ms slightly for narrow-latency-sensitive models to reduce kernel flip thrash (trade p50 for p99).
- Add a short 'sticky' bias to fused kernel choice for sequences that recently ran fused ops (avoid flip flops within X seconds).
- Instrument lightweight kernel-choice audit logs (already implemented in pr/1427) and expose a dashboard for per-model kernel churn.
- Experiment with adaptive prefetch_window_ms: widen during bursts automatically when kernel_handoffs > threshold.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How often do handoffs occur in production traffic versus our synthetic bursts? Need a sample from production traces (ask SRE for 24h sample).
- Are there particular model layer shapes or kv_cache sizes that correlate strongly with flip rate?
- Can batching coalescer incorporate sequence-length-aware heuristics? (simple: partition short vs long queues for separate coalescing paths)

Notes to self / TODOs:
- [ ] Push microdriver artifact with trace hooks to staging CI (Jon)
- [ ] Add a lightweight dashboard panel for kernel_handoffs per-model (Lina)
- [ ] Run one 24h sampling job on hosted-api tail cluster and share anonymized trace sample (Pavel)
- [ ] Draft short RFC for sticky-kernel-bias heuristic (this doc -> RFC)

Useful references (internal):
- Confluence: /display/INFR/Kernel+Selection+Audit (private)
- Jira: INFR-812 (regression), INFR-830 (coalescer improvements)
- GH PR: runtime#1427 (kernel-choice instrumentation)

Appendix: quick checklist for triage when customer reports sporadic tail spikes
1) Ask for request timestamps and sample request ids -> get trace ids.
2) Pull per-request kernel tags for that time window.
3) If kernel handoffs visible, check kv_eviction and prefetch counts.
4) Try increasing coalescer_delay_ms by 2–4ms in a canary and measure p99.
5) If canary improves, propose sticky-bias experiment and gradual rollout.

End of notebook. Keep this short and mutated; aim to run any of these three recipes in <10m of setup time.

Comments welcome — particularly on the sticky-bias idea and whether we should implement at scheduler or kernel-selection layer.
